Subject: BeaconCare SIG — follow-up on RTO/RPO and evidence

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the initial SIG submission — your team moved quickly and we appreciate it. A few items need clarifying before our security review can sign off:

1) Can you confirm objective RTO and RPO targets for the hosted Redwood API under the Dedicated plan (per-region)? We need this phrased as measurable SLAs.
2) Backup details: frequency, retention, encryption-at-rest details, and which data classes are included (configs, KV caches, user prompts).
3) Regional failover: what automatic failover behaviors exist for cross-region outage vs. regional maintenance? Are warm standby regions maintained?
4) Evidence: we requested runbooks and a recent DR rehearsal report. Can you point to the artifacts or attach redacted versions?

We'd like to get these answered before our security call Friday. Attaching the SIG worksheet with line items highlighted.

Thanks — can you and your operations lead respond with specifics and any attachments?

Emma

Sr. InfoSec Program Manager, BeaconCare

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: BeaconCare SIG — follow-up on RTO/RPO and evidence

Emma — thanks for the clear list. See answers below (summary first, artifacts attached & linked). I’ve kept the language suitable for inclusion in your SIG response.

Summary (measurable):
- Per-region production RTO: 10 minutes for control-plane detection + automated routing; full request-level failover within 60s for active-configured routes when using regional routing policies.
- RPO: best-effort for in-flight tokens; persistent customer data (model inputs/outputs when enabled) retained with RPO = 15 minutes with our default snapshot cadence.

Detailed responses: 
1) RTO / RPO (Dedicated offering, per-region):
  - RTO (detection + automated routing): 10 minutes median for detection and triggering routing policies; customer-visible request retry typically reroutes within ~60s when using built-in client SDK retries and regional routing.
  - RTO (full recovery to warm standby): 4 hours for stateful capacity rehydration in a warm-standby region when cross-region capacity must be reprovisioned.
  - RPO: for persisted customer artifacts (optional request logging/diagnostics), snapshots are taken every 15 minutes. KV cache for active sessions is best-effort replication; when customers enable cross-region replication RPO is reduced to <1 minute for persistent state.

2) Backups & retention:
  - Configuration & metadata: immediate point-in-time snapshots written to encrypted object storage every 15 minutes; retained 90 days by default (adjustable via account settings).
  - Model binaries: immutable, versioned artifacts stored across regions; retention = model owner policy (default 1 year).
  - Logs & telemetry: 30 days stored in hot tier (retention expandable).
  - Encryption: all backups encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS) or Redwood-managed keys; TLS 1.2+ in transit.
  - Data classes: configs, deployment manifests, customer-owned prompts/logs (only if customer enables request logging), and audit logs are included. KV caches are not durable unless the customer opts into persistence.

3) Regional failover & modes:
  - Active-active model: customers can configure regional active-active routing for latency-sensitive workloads; requests are served locally with automatic routing rules.
  - Active-passive (automatic failover): when a region reports unhealthy, our control plane routes traffic to the next healthy region per customer routing policy. Detection uses multi-signal health checks (control-plane telemetry + dataplane error rates).
  - Warm standby: Dedicated customers may opt for warm-standby regions where a minimal pool is kept warmed with pre-loaded model caches; warm-standby reprovisioning (scale-up to full capacity) target: 4 hours.
  - Cold reprovisioning: if no warm standby is configured, full reprovisioning target depends on instance availability and can be 12+ hours.

4) Evidence & runbooks:
  - Attached: BeaconCare_SIG_RTO_RPO_Evidence.pdf (redacted recent DR rehearsal notes), runbook-snapshot-20260110.txt (excerpt of on-call steps and failover checklist), s3-lifecycle-policy.json (example retention policy).
  - Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/BeaconCare/SIG/RTO-RPO-evidence
  - We also have an internal post-mortem template and a recent tabletop report; we can provide a redacted tabletop summary on request.

Testing cadence & governance:
  - Scheduled failover drills: quarterly for Dedicated customers by default; annual full disaster recovery rehearsal across regions. We record outcomes and retention windows in the governance dashboard.
  - Runbook ownership: runbooks are maintained by SRE on the serving runtime team; customer-facing runbooks (high-level) are provided as part of the onboarding package.

Next steps / suggested artifacts to share with your GRC team:
  - Redacted DR rehearsal summary (we can redact IPs and customer IDs) — attach if helpful.
  - Example canary rollback timeline for A/B rollouts.
  - Confirmation of KMS usage and options (we support CMKs and HSM-backed KMS).

I’ve looped in Dylan (sales lead) and Markus (SRE) if you want a quick 30-minute sync to walk through the artifacts before Friday.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Security & Compliance (Solutions)
